body.heading: The all-or-nothing trap
paragraphs: It is easy to believe exercise only counts if it is long, strenuous and done in special clothes. That belief quietly cancels a lot of good movement: the walk to the shop, the stairs, the gardening, the dancing in the kitchen.
Bodies respond to regular, moderate movement too. A daily pattern you enjoy will do more for you than an intense plan you abandon in a fortnight.

body.heading: Sneak movement into the day
paragraphs: Attach movement to things you already do: a short walk after lunch, stretching while the kettle boils, taking the long way to the printer. Small, frequent and pleasant beats rare and punishing.
Pay attention to what your own body reports: energy, stiffness, mood, sleep. Let that feedback, rather than guilt, shape how much you do, and build up gradually if you want more.

takeaway: Choose movement you enjoy enough to repeat, and let it count.
